tokenizer.d: The fixed program that chops text into tokens before the model sees it: common words, pieces of rare words, punctuation, and spaces glued to the next word.

residual sublayer.d: One step of the form y ↦ y + φ(y): read the state, compute a branch φ, add it back. Each Qwen decoder block has two: a token mixer, then a SwiGLU MLP.

decoder block.d: One repeated unit of the model: a token mixer sublayer followed by an MLP sublayer. “Layer ℓ” means the residual state after block ℓ. Qwen3.6-27B has 64 of them.

token mixer.d: The sublayer that moves information between positions. In the Qwen models used here it is gated softmax attention in one block of four and Gated DeltaNet in the others.

Gated DeltaNet.d: A token mixer that keeps a fixed-size memory matrix, updated once per position: fade the old memory, then write the new value under the new key, correcting what was stored under it. Later positions read it with a query.

query, key and value.d: The three vectors attention makes from each position. The query is the question asked by the reading position, keys are the labels of earlier positions, values are what they hand over. Score = query · key.

attention weight.d: How much a reading position takes from each earlier position. Scores are query · key divided by √(head size); a softmax turns them into weights that are positive and add to 1.

causal mask.d: The rule that a position may only read itself and earlier positions, never later ones. So a change at position p can only affect positions p and after.

RoPE.d: Rotary position embedding: queries and keys are rotated by angles that depend on their position, so the attention score depends on how far apart two tokens are.

softmax temperature.d: A number τ that every score is divided by before softmax. Below 1 it sharpens the distribution, above 1 it flattens it. It is a sampling setting and plays no part in the lenses.

gate read.d: In a SwiGLU neuron, the number z = w_gate · x̃ that goes through silu and acts as a soft on/off switch for the neuron's output.

up read.d: In a SwiGLU neuron, the second linear read m = w_up · x̃, multiplied by silu of the gate read. The product of the two reads is what makes the neuron curved.

write direction.d: The fixed direction w_down along which an MLP neuron adds its output back into the residual stream.

bilinear.d: A function that is a product of two linear reads, (a·x)(b·x). Its Hessian is the constant matrix abᵀ + baᵀ. A SwiGLU neuron becomes bilinear if silu is replaced by the identity.

cross-entropy.d: The average of minus the log-likelihood of the true next tokens, in nats. Training a language model means making it small.

valid positions.d: The positions 16 to T − 2 of each window that the J-lens and H-lens average over. Early positions act as attention sinks with atypical statistics; the last has no next-token target.

attention sink.d: An early position that attention heads put weight on when they have nothing better to read. Its residual statistics are unusual, so the lenses skip the first 16 positions.

verbalisable.d: Readable as words: decoding a direction through a lens gives a ranked token list that a person can name, like a list of city names.

read direction.d: For the J-lens at layer ℓ, the vector r_t = J_ℓᵀ u_t: the layer-ℓ direction that, on average, pushes the output towards token t. The lens score is r_t · h.

activation unit.d: The arbitrary unit in which a model's internal numbers are stored. It has no physical meaning, but every residual coordinate shares it, so comparisons between coordinates are meaningful.
